revisions.revision_reason: Replace a universal mandatory field list with an explicit profile-declared dependency denominator and typed applicability states.
revisions.normative_voice: An Evaluation Binding is the immutable identity-and-state set for every dependency that one evaluation profile declares applicable, together with the complete declared denominator that makes omitted, inapplicable, missing, invalid, and bound dependencies distinguishable.
revisions.formal_voice: EvaluationBinding = (profile_ref, denominator, dependency_bindings, dependency_states, created_at, expires_at, invalidation_keys, supersedes_ref), where for every d in denominator, state(d) is one of {bound, inapplicable, missing, invalid}; evaluable only if every required applicable d is bound, current, and valid.
revisions.plain_language_voice: Freeze the full checklist for this kind of evaluation, mark what applies, and bind every required item. Do not force irrelevant fields, and do not let an omitted field look inapplicable.
revisions.domain_context_voice: An ORODI deployment evaluation can require artifact, environment, authorization, observer, and pre/post-state bindings without inventing a topology or fixture dependency when its selected profile declares those inapplicable.
revisions.boundary: A complete Evaluation Binding proves denominator and identity completeness only; it does not prove source authenticity, evidence truth, policy correctness, owner acceptance, or effect authority.

revisions.revision_reason: Name the exact evidence facet instead of claiming one universal state vocabulary for model coverage, availability, validation, and obligation status.
revisions.normative_voice: Operational Evidence Evaluation State is the disjoint typed condition assigned to one evaluated operational obligation: passed, failed, missing, invalid, inconclusive, stale, or not-run.
revisions.formal_voice: OperationalEvidenceEvaluationState is one of {passed, failed, missing, invalid, inconclusive, stale, not-run}; the set is pairwise disjoint, and an aggregate may be passed only when every required denominator member is present, valid, fresh, executed, and passed.
revisions.plain_language_voice: For one operational check, success, failure, no data, bad data, old data, uncertainty, and never run are different answers. Other questions, such as model coverage, may use their own states.
revisions.domain_context_voice: ORODI uses this state only for evaluated operational obligations; model coverage, evidence availability, validator result, lifecycle state, and owner decision remain separate owner-defined facets.
revisions.boundary: This vocabulary must not flatten model coverage, evidence availability, validation result, lifecycle state, or owner decision into one state machine; absence of failure is never passed.

revisions.revision_reason: Replace fixed universal type names with owner-defined semantic roles that preserve local domain vocabulary.
revisions.normative_voice: Failure Meaning Separation is the invariant that subject-level failure meaning, boundary or integration outcome, and runtime exception remain distinct owner-defined roles throughout evaluation and recovery.
revisions.formal_voice: SubjectFailureRole != BoundaryOutcomeRole != RuntimeExceptionRole; map(RuntimeExceptionRole, profile_owner) -> BoundaryOutcomeRole and interpret(BoundaryOutcomeRole, subject_owner) -> optional SubjectFailureRole; each owner controls its vocabulary and neither mapping redefines the target role.
revisions.plain_language_voice: What failed for the business, what the boundary reported, and what the runtime threw may be connected, but they are not interchangeable and need not share universal type names.
revisions.domain_context_voice: ORODI profiles map tool and runtime exceptions into boundary outcomes while the owning domain decides whether those outcomes establish a subject-level failure and who may continue or recover.
revisions.boundary: A runtime exception cannot create subject meaning, a boundary outcome cannot silently become an owner decision, and a subject failure does not prescribe one exception, retry, or integration vocabulary.

consumer_drift.reason: The immutable predecessor language still names the original candidate terms and must not be silently rewritten before a digest-bound promotion decision.
The human language guide remains bound to the predecessor candidate epoch.

claim_ceiling: These successor candidates answer the D48 semantic challenges only. They do not revise the immutable predecessor pack, allocate canonical identifiers, promote definitions, or authorize downstream construction.
